holidays.name: National Donut Day (First Friday of June)
holidays.description: A sprinkle-covered celebration of the glorious fried ring of dough, when bakeries hand out free donuts and everyone pretends it's a perfectly reasonable breakfast, lunch, and dinner.
holidays.origin: Started in 1938 by the Salvation Army in Chicago to honor the volunteers known as 'Doughnut Lassies' who served donuts to soldiers in World War I, and to raise funds during the Great Depression.
holidays.funFact: The Doughnut Lassies fried donuts in soldiers' helmets in the trenches of France when they ran out of proper cooking equipment.

holidays.name: World Milk Day
holidays.description: A global toast to all things moo-juice, with dairy lovers raising glasses of milk (and cheese, and yogurt) in honor of the white stuff.
holidays.origin: Established by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations in 2001 to recognize the importance of milk as a global food and to promote the dairy sector.
holidays.funFact: Cows can produce around 6 to 7 gallons of milk a day, and the cow-to-milk ratio means one cow can fill roughly 100 glasses daily.

holidays.name: Say Something Nice Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to complimenting strangers, coworkers, and even your cat. Warning: side effects include unexpected smiles and awkward but heartwarming eye contact.
holidays.origin: Created in 1980s by Chase's Calendar of Events-style observances and popularized as a way to boost positivity, encouraging people to say something kind to at least three people.
holidays.funFact: Studies on gratitude and compliments suggest that the person giving the compliment often feels just as happy as the one receiving it.

holidays.name: Hug Your Cat Day
holidays.description: A day for cat owners to squeeze their feline overlords, provided the cats consent. Scratch levels may vary and negotiations may be required.
holidays.origin: An unofficial pet holiday that emerged from the internet-era boom in cat appreciation days, giving cat lovers yet another excuse to cuddle.
holidays.funFact: A cat's purr vibrates at 25 to 150 Hertz, a frequency range that some researchers say may promote healing in bones and tissue.

holidays.name: Flip a Coin Day
holidays.description: A day to let fate decide everything from lunch choices to life decisions, all by tossing a little piece of metal into the air.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance celebrating the age-old practice of coin tossing, which dates back to ancient Rome, where it was called 'navia aut caput' (ship or head).
holidays.funFact: Research from Stanford suggests a coin toss lands on the same side it started on about 51% of the time.
